newsitem.title: HAITI: Proposed Haiti budget includes pension for soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Proposed Haiti budget includes pension for soldiers.

text.p: Haiti's parliament on Friday began debating a proposed government budget, which includes pensions for soldiers who lost their jobs when former President Jean-Bertrand Aristide disbanded the army.
The budget proposal before the chamber of deputies includes $3.6 million for soldiers who were part of the Haitian army until it was abolished in 1995.

Aristide disbanded the military upon his return to power by U.S. troops after three years of military rule in which an estimated 5,000 people died. Many of the former soldiers have been demonstrating to receive their pensions during the past two years.

U.N. officials have said that violence against police officers and attacks on government buildings stopped once the government indicated in September that the ex-soldiers would receive some compensation.
"Not all of the soldiers will receive pension money," Justice Minister Max Antoine told reporters, without elaborating on who would and would not be paid.

Haiti's lower house met on Friday to begin debating a proposed overall budget of $893 million, which officials said is based on the assumption that Haiti will receive hundreds of millions of dollars of international aid because of parliament's recent approval of a privatisation scheme.
Deputy Alix Fils-Aime, a member of the Finance and Budget Commission, said some 65 percent of the budget will be financed by international aid in the form of loans and donations.
Parliament is not expected to finalise the spending plan until the end of the month.
The proposed budget is divided between $333 million for general operations, and more than $500 million for investment.
